tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In respect of AY 2017-18, the Assessing officer vide order dated 30th March, 2024 made additions of Rs. 184.99 Crores under section 115JB of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (‘the Act’) and disallowed expenses to the extent of Rs. 1.51 Crores, under normal provisions of the Act, thereby raising a tax demand of Rs. 73.04 Crores. The Company duly filed an appeal before the CIT (Appeals) against the said order. The CIT(Appeals) after perusing the submissions filed by the Company, vide its order, has decided the appeal in favour of the Company.
tax_litigation.status: The tax demand of Rs. 73.04 Crores, as raised by AO earlier, was duly disclosed as contingent liability in the Balance Sheet. Since the appeal has now been decided in favour of the Company, such tax demand would no longer be payable by the Company.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The SLP is filed by Samsung India Electronics along with many other entities from West Bengal, challenging the order dated 30.01.2025 of Calcutta High Court whereby the High Court uphold the constitutional validity of the “West Bengal Taxes on Entry of Goods into the Local Areas” Act, 2012 as amended by the “West Bengal Finance Act 2017” and the rules made thereunder. Websol filed Intervening Application (IA) No. 119258/2025 to be impleaded as party to the said SLP as Websol received demand notices for the payment of entry tax for the FY 2015-2016, 2016-2017 and 2017-2018 having cumulative demand of Rs 8,97,77,631.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The State of West Bengal and Ors.
tax_litigation.status: The main parties in the SLP Samsung India and Pepsico Holding who challenged the Order of the Hon’ble Calcutta High Court, have sought for the settlement under the West Bengal Sales Tax (Settlement of Dispute) Act, 2025 and it’s amendment in terms TRADE CIRCULAR NO. 01/2025 DATED: 04/08/2025. In furtherance to the legal opinion from our counsel and considering the fact that Websol had not been a party to the matter before Division Bench in Calcutta High Court, and the main parties had withdrawn their cases and opted to go for settlement, we also withdrawn our matter from the Supreme Court and opted for the settlement under the WB Settlement of Dispute Act and TRADE CIRCULAR NO. 01/2025 DATED: 04/08/2025.
